title: Luigi Mangione expected to plead guilty during Manhattan federal court hearing
---
<p>The man charged with gunning down United Healthcare CEO Brian Thompson on a New York City street two years ago is <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/luigi-mangione-expected-plead-guilty-new-york-federal-case-rcna592221">expected to plead guilty to stalking charges</a> in Manhattan federal court Friday, according to sources familiar with the matter.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/luigi-mangione-trials-cases-court-when-date-charges-prison-what-know-rcna257102">Luigi Mangione</a>, 28, has a pretrial conference scheduled for 11 a.m.</p>
<p>The terms of a potential plea agreement remain unclear. Sources familiar with the matter said Thursday that negotiations were ongoing and nothing was final until Mangione accepted a deal. That potential decision could be reversed during the hearing.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/luigi-mangione-insurance-murder-brian-thompson-rcna347942?utm_source=NBC&amp;utm_medium=iframely">A killing spurs contempt: The tip line that shaped Luigi Mangione’s murder case</a></p>
<p>“You can’t have seen death like that and sanctify somebody who does that,” one former investigator said.</p>
<figure><a href="https://www.nbcnews.com"><img src="https://iframe.nbcnews.com/pj?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnodeassets.nbcnews.com%2Fcdnassets%2Fprojects%2Framen%2Ffavicon%2Fnbcnews%2Fall-other-sizes-PNG.ico%2Ffavicon-32x32.png&amp;key=306c794165a723f0954b3672a2972d184b8375ec&amp;cache=temp-raw&amp;background=%23fff"/></a></figure>
<p><a href="https://www.nbcnews.com">NBC Newsnbcnews.com</a>/Jun 6</p>
<p>Federal prosecutors and defense attorneys declined to comment Thursday.</p>
<p>Mangione was charged with two federal counts — interstate stalking resulting in death and stalking through use of interstate facilities resulting in death — though it isn’t clear if he will plead guilty to both. The charges carry a maximum penalty of life in prison and are separate from the state allegations, which include second-degree murder and firearms crimes.</p>

<p>What Luigi Mangione could gain from plea negotiations</p>
<p>00:0000:00</p>
<p>Mangione’s trial in the state case is expected to begin early next month.</p>
<p>He pleaded not guilty in both cases and previously faced two additional federal counts, including using a firearm to commit murder, which carried a maximum penalty of death. A judge dismissed that charge earlier this year.</p>
<p>The brazen killing of Thompson — a father of two who led the nation’s largest healthcare insurer — put a spotlight on the country’s <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/ceo-shooting-health-insurance-frustration-denied-claims-rcna183805">health insurance industry and</a> <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/ceo-shooting-health-insurance-frustration-denied-claims-rcna183805">widespread frustration over denied claims</a>.</p>
<p>Mangione was arrested at a Pennsylvania McDonald’s on Dec. 9, 2024, five days after Thompson was fatally shot outside a Manhattan hotel that was hosting an investors’ conference.</p>
<p>Among the pieces of evidence found by authorities in Mangione’s backpack was a notebook that detailed his apparent grievances against the industry. At the scene, authorities found a bullet and two shell casings that had the words “delay,” “deny,” “depose” written on them.</p>
<p>Mangione’s attorneys had sought to bar the notebook from being introduced as evidence at his trials, arguing authorities obtained it during an illegal search. Judges in both cases rejected that argument.</p>
